title: Tool run (bench-run record)
description: ADR-0007. Immutable, append-only record of ONE invocation of ONE Tool on ONE input by the executor run-button (req #15, smallest form). The CANONICAL counterpart of a `run_record` for value-NEUTRAL bench operations: 'run the IA-Cloud Tool on seed 39'. Distinct from `run_record` on purpose — a Tool run has NO hypothesis and NO confirmed/refuted status (a Tool is a capability, not a bet), so it must not pollute the experiment corpus that drives claim blast-radius. It IS first-class provenance: it stamps the Tool version + the content hash IN FORCE at run time (so a later substrate bump makes a prior tool_run's hash stale and visible), and claims/goals MAY cite a tool_run id. The drift-check (tool_lint) runs BEFORE invocation; a stale binding yields status='drift_refused' and the bound code is never run.

id.description: Bench-run id: 'tr_' + tool id + '_' + a run timestamp/counter, lowercase underscore. Stable forever; may be cited by claims/goals as provenance.

tool.description: substrate_component id of the Tool that was run. Referential: must resolve to a substrate_component.

tool_version.description: The Tool's current_version at run time. Referential: must appear in that component's versions[]. With hash_at_run, this is the reproducibility + drift stamp.

hash_at_run.description: Content hash of the bound source file at run time ('sha256:...', the tool_lint format). Compared to the card's current_hash to detect a silent change. Null only for a drift_refused run where the file vanished.

hash_ok.description: True iff hash_at_run matched the Tool card's current_hash (binding was in-sync). False with status='ok' is possible only if --force overrode a drift refusal (recorded honestly).

status.description: ok = the Tool ran to completion. drift_refused = the drift-check (tool_lint) failed and the bound code was NOT run (entry_point missing or hash moved). error = the Tool was invoked but raised (see `error`).

input.description: The input the Tool was run ON (the artifact side of the call), e.g. {seed: 39, epoch: 12} or {lc_path: '...'}. Freeform; the executor records exactly what it passed.

params.description: Effective parameters used = the Tool card's default_params overlaid with the run's overrides. The full, reproducible parameterisation (the ADR-0007 'variation lives in params' record).

metrics.description: Open metric bag summarising the output (e.g. return-value shapes/keys, counts, a scalar result, wall_s). The dashboard indexes whatever is present.

wall_s.description: Wall-clock seconds the invocation took (null for drift_refused).

artefacts.description: Output files produced (saved arrays, plots). Plots surface to the web-app plot stream tagged by this tool_run. Same shape as run_record.artefacts.

caption.description: One-line caption for the plot stream.

artifacts_produced.description: ADR-0007. artifact_instance ids reified from this run's port-typed outputs ('recognised materials only'). Referential: each must resolve to an artifact_instance. Distinct from `artefacts` (figures/logs): these are addressable, typed MATERIALS on the laboratory shelf.

oracle_clean.description: True iff no truth_* / oracle data was read during the run. A Tool like load_truth reads oracle data by definition -> false. Mirrors run_record.oracle_clean so a bench run is honest about provenance.

error.description: For status='error', the exception type + message (and short traceback tail). For status='drift_refused', the human-readable reason the binding was rejected. Null for status='ok'.

reason.description: Operator note: WHY this Tool was run on this input (the bench-log annotation). Free text.

commit.description: git SHA the run executed at (reproducibility).

source.description: How the run-button was triggered: a terminal CLI invocation, the dashboard run-button (via the intent queue), or a spine skill.

executed_at.description: When the compute actually ran, if different from created_at.
